quandoUsar: Long product descriptions, bios, or reviews in a list, clipped to a few lines with `lines`.
Variable-length texts where the button should only appear when the text actually exceeds the clip.
Paragraphs with links in the middle: the whole text stays in the DOM, and a link hidden below the clip opens the text when it receives focus.
quandoEvitar: Use `collapsible` when the hidden part is a separate block, such as a list or a form, and not the continuation of the text.
Use `accordion` for several sections with their own titles.

teclado.acao: On the button, opens or closes the text.
When focus reaches a link hidden below the clip, the text opens on its own.

acessibilidade: The button has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the two labels share the same space and the inactive one is hidden, so the name read is always the current one.
The clipped text stays whole in the DOM, available to the screen reader; the clip is only visual.
movimento: The height slides with a smooth deceleration, 500 to 600 ms on open and 400 to 450 ms on close, depending on the distance; the fade on the last line goes away along with it and the arrow rotates in step.
When closing with the start of the text off screen, the page scrolls back to it.
With “reduce motion” on, the text opens and closes instantly, the labels swap without a transition, and the scroll back is instant.
responsivo: At rest, the clip is CSS in `lh`, and an observer remeasures when the width or font changes: the button appears or disappears depending on whether the text exceeds the clip.
desempenho: Each instance uses a `ResizeObserver` to know whether the text overflows; in a long list, that is one observer per item.
notasIA: Translate the labels with `moreLabel` and `lessLabel`; the defaults are “Read more” and “Show less”.
Do not draw your own “read more”: the button already appears only when the text exceeds `lines` lines (default 3).
To control it, pass `expanded` with `onExpandedChange`. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/expandable-text/expandable-text`.
